## Overview

This dataset contains time-series data representing the electrical and environmental behavior of a small-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) system.

The dataset is designed for research, prototyping, and educational purposes in areas such as:

* Solar fault detection
* Predictive maintenance
* TinyML / Edge AI deployment
* Time-series anomaly detection
* Energy analytics

The data simulates realistic PV system dynamics including irradiance variation, temperature effects, cloud disturbances, sensor noise, and multiple types of abnormal operating conditions.

---

## System Model

The  PV system represents a low-power standalone solar panel setup (e.g., 12V–24V system), commonly used in:

* Remote sensing installations
* Off-grid energy systems
* IoT power units
* Educational laboratory environments

Physical relationships such as irradiance-current proportionality and temperature-dependent voltage variation are incorporated into the data generation process.

---

## Dataset Features

| Feature     | Description                                                           |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| irradiance  | Simulated solar irradiance (W/m²) with cloud disturbance noise        |
| temperature | PV module temperature (°C) including environmental variability        |
| voltage     | Panel output voltage (V) with thermal and sensor noise effects        |
| current     | Panel output current (A) proportional to irradiance with disturbances |
| power       | Computed electrical power (Voltage × Current)                         |
| fault       | Binary anomaly label (0 = normal operation, 1 = abnormal condition)   |

---

## Anomaly Simulation

The dataset includes randomly injected abnormal conditions such as:

* Partial shading events (sudden current reduction)
* Open-circuit or loose connection scenarios
* Sensor spikes and measurement noise bursts
* Voltage oscillations
* Short duration performance degradation patterns

These anomalies are intended to support development and benchmarking of:

* Supervised classification models
* Unsupervised anomaly detection models
* TinyML autoencoder architectures
* Edge inference pipelines

---

## Intended Applications

This dataset is suitable for:

* Machine learning model training and evaluation
* Real-time anomaly detection research
* Edge AI deployment prototyping (e.g., microcontrollers such as ESP32)
* Feature engineering experimentation
* Digital twin modeling studies

---

## License

Recommended: CC BY 4.0 or MIT License (depending on your preference).
